full_judgment:
2. Opposite party No. 1 instituted Title Suit No. 16 of 1992 against the petitioner namely Mrs. Nazma Begum and others for a declaration of her title to and recovery of khas possession in the suit property. 

 9. The learned Subordinate Judge passed the judgment on 27.9.98 where after the decree was prepared and signed on 6.10.98. The decree was drawn in accordance with the order portion of the judgment i.e. in the decree plaintiffs title was declared and nothing was said about the prayer for recovery of khas possession. Opposite party No.1 Arzuda Khatun on 8.11.98 filed an application before the learned Subordinate Judge praying for amendment of the judgment and the decree incorporating the relief of khas possession in her favour and the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 12.11.98 allowed the prayer for amendment of the judgment and decree accordingly and it appears from the record that the judgment and the decree were amended. 

 24. I have been informed at the time of hearing this revisional application by the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner that the petitioner has also preferred an appeal against the connected judgment and decree. It is apparent from the earlier discussion that the petitioner would not be prejudiced by the impugned order amending the judgment and decree. On the other hand, the decree originally passed in favour of opposite party No. 1 declaring her title without recovery of khas possession will be of no use to her. The learned Subordinate Judge, as a matter of prudence, ought to have served a copy of the petition for amendment upon the petitioner or upon her advocate but his failure to do so cannot be said to have rendered the impugned order illegal and void.
